Package com.splendor.util

Class InputResolver

java.lang.Object
com.splendor.util.InputResolver
public class InputResolver extends Object
Robust input parsing and validation utility for console-based user interaction. This class provides a safe wrapper around Scanner to handle user input with comprehensive validation, error recovery, and helpful error messages. It prevents common input-related crashes such as InputMismatchException and NoSuchElementException.

Key features:

  • Range-bounded integer input with automatic re-prompting
  • String length validation with min/max constraints
  • Yes/no confirmation prompts with flexible input parsing
  • Undo/back signal support via "Z" or "UNDO" keywords
  • Invisible Unicode control character sanitization
  • Optional callback on invalid input for UI refresh

All prompting methods handle the full input loop internally, continuing to prompt until valid input is received or an undo signal is given.

Example usage: 

   InputResolver resolver = new InputResolver();
   int choice = resolver.promptForInt("Enter choice (1-4): ", 1, 4);
   String name = resolver.promptForString("Enter name: ", 1, 20);
   boolean confirmed = resolver.promptForConfirmation("Confirm?");

    • promptForInt

      public int promptForInt(String prompt, int minValue, int maxValue, Runnable onInvalid)
      Prompts for and parses an integer with an optional callback invoked each time the user enters an out-of-range or non-numeric value. Entering "Z" or "UNDO" (case-insensitive) returns -1 immediately so callers can treat it as a back/undo signal without looping.
      Parameters:
      prompt - Prompt text printed before every input attempt.
      minValue - Inclusive lower bound for accepted values.
      maxValue - Inclusive upper bound for accepted values.
      onInvalid - Optional Runnable called before re-printing the prompt after bad input (e.g., to re-render the game screen). May be null.
      Returns:
      Valid integer in [minValue, maxValue], or -1 for undo/back.
